external_entities.name: customer
external_entities.description: Customer who browses and places orders through the mobile app and receives a fax confirmation.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app
external_entities.notes: The source does not describe the customer's authentication or device security.

external_entities.name: marketing
external_entities.description: Marketing staff who maintain the catalogue in a spreadsheet.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Marketing keep the catalogue in a spreadsheet.
external_entities.notes: The source does not state whether Marketing is represented by a specific identity or access-control mechanism.

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: Mobile application through which customers browse and order socks.
processes.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app
processes.notes: The source says there is no website.

processes.name: web API
processes.description: API used by the mobile app, storing customer information and handing orders to SIMS.
processes.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database
processes.notes: Nobody here can tell me what the API does about authentication.

processes.name: SIMS
processes.description: Stock and inventory system that receives orders, stores delivery addresses in a flat file, and sends dispatch notes to the fax gateway.
processes.source_excerpt: SIMS does two things with an order.
processes.notes: The source says SIMS has been running since long before the app existed.

processes.name: fax gateway
processes.description: Gateway that receives dispatch notes and faxes customer confirmations.
processes.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway, which faxes the customer a confirmation
processes.notes: The gateway dials the number stored against the order, and nobody checks it arrived at the right place.

processes.name: macros
processes.description: Spreadsheet macros that send SQL statements directly to the web API to change prices and product copy.
processes.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy
processes.notes: The macros are described as a stopgap that is still in use.

data_stores.name: user database
data_stores.description: Database containing customer names, addresses, and the card they paid with.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with.
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me whether the user database is encrypted.

data_stores.name: flat file
data_stores.description: Flat file kept alongside SIMS containing delivery addresses only.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file kept alongside it — only addresses go in that file, nothing else
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me whether the flat file is encrypted.

data_stores.name: spreadsheet
data_stores.description: Spreadsheet containing the marketing catalogue and macros that change prices and product copy through the web API.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Marketing keep the catalogue in a spreadsheet.
data_stores.notes: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

trust_boundaries.name: customer device
trust_boundaries.description: Customer-controlled device hosting the mobile app.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app
trust_boundaries.notes: The device boundary is inferred from the mobile-app customer interaction.

trust_boundaries.name: office
trust_boundaries.description: Office environment containing the marketing laptop, spreadsheet, API, SIMS, databases, flat file, macros, and fax gateway.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.
trust_boundaries.notes: The source explicitly places the marketing laptop in the office but does not describe further network segmentation.

assumptions.assumption: The web API is reachable from outside the office because customers use the online mobile app to access it.
assumptions.basis: The description says Sokify sells socks online, customers use the mobile app, and the app talks to the web API.

assumptions.assumption: The user database is confidential because it contains customer names, addresses, and payment-card information.
assumptions.basis: The stated contents are personal and payment data.

assumptions.assumption: The flat file is confidential because it contains customer delivery addresses.
assumptions.basis: The stated contents are personal data.

assumptions.assumption: The customer device is controlled by a different party from Sokify.
assumptions.basis: Customers use the mobile app on their own customer devices; the text does not describe those devices as controlled by Sokify.
